candidate=false. The submitted supporting proof chain contains a concrete mathematical defect: BJ v4 Lemma 4.6 is false in its stated generality. This audit establishes no counterexample to the prescribed-reference equation theorem itself.

The defect is independently verifiable. Let K be the disjoint union of an isolated point q and a convergent sequence {p_j} with limit p∞. Set S=N_{>0}, T=R and ρ(n)=1/n. For each n, let F_n consist of the functions f_{n,m,c}, with m∈N_{>0} and c∈R, taking value c at q, −∞ at p_n, and c−m everywhere else. These functions are extended-valued continuous, and F_n is stable under addition of constants. For every fixed n, f_{n,m,0} decreases to the same continuous function g, where g(q)=0 and g=−∞ on the sequence and its limit. Thus g belongs to every closure F̃_{1/n}; the constant decreasing net g_n=g meets the lemma's hypotheses with 1/n→0.

Nevertheless F̃_0 is empty. In any decreasing net of functions from these families, select one term belonging to F_n. Its value at p_n is −∞, so every later term must also belong to F_n: functions from every other family are finite at p_n. Consequently ρ is constantly 1/n on that entire tail and cannot converge to zero. This disproves the asserted flattening lemma, even with a nonidentically −∞ normalized limit.

The freshly opened proof contains the corresponding error. Its strict inequality (4.5) fails where both sides are −∞; the asserted strictly negative exponential difference can instead be zero. Exact public coordinates are BJ v4 L3187–3198@P45 for the statement, L3222–3241@P45–46 for the faulty directedness argument, and L3264–3270@P46 for its application to Theorem 4.5. Theorem 4.15(i) explicitly invokes Lemma 4.6 at L3550@P49; Corollary 6.17 then invokes Theorem 4.15(i) at L4559–4565@P65. Draft §4.2 needs this nonample homogeneous approximation. Draft §10 also uses the varying-class closure theorem in establishing the zero-class cone. G0 grants the actual ample domain and does not grant these nonample applications. A valid replacement in the actual Fubini–Study setting requires a new argument. The topological counterexample does not assert that the specialized algebraic closure theorem is false.

I checked the remaining manuscript against its full stated scope. The no-Bertini Kodaira realization in §3 correctly covers every big actual rational L under the retained hypotheses, including the nonreduced hyperplane section argument. The compactness repair for divided approximants in §4.2 is valid conditional on the required genuine homogeneous approximation. Divisorial determination correctly supplies the unique original-carrier quotient and values at the fixed poles, once the cone identity is established.

Conditional on that genuine cone identity and the scoped foundations, §§5–9 correctly transport the equation theory. The plus sign in the frame identity is correct. Local multiplication by the divisor section identifies the metrics on U before targets are selected. The bounded products, reference truncations, mixed polarization and zero pluripolar mass arguments identify the operator with the genuine ample quotient product and retain raw mass A^n. The quotient-integral energy and target criterion retain the fixed datum. The envelope inequalities, continuous two-sided derivatives, compactness, bounded-J target continuity, attained variational maximum, comparison, domination and all-point uniqueness have the required signs and hypotheses. No countability, finite-generation or prescribed-support restriction enters these deductions. Absolute integrability of σ is appropriately not asserted.

For the actual trivial bundle, the zero-mass equation calculations are correct once PSH(0)=R is established: the only positive target is zero, the raw energy and top product vanish, and constants are unique modulo constants. The supplied proof of the constants-only cone relies on the unrepaired closure chain. Both diagnostics in §11 are correct: H+aE has positive section volume despite nonpositive self-intersection for suitable a, whereas the semiample bundle on P1×P1 gives genuine zero-volume noninjectivity. Neither diagnostic completes the original equation axis.

Harmless wording corrections: BJ 7.23 is a Remark. Formula (5.9) is an alternating polarization identity whose resulting mixed measure is positive; its coefficients are not all positive. These wording changes do not repair the foundational defect.

The public statement and pertinent proof bodies were opened in the specified versions: BJ 1801.08229v4, BJ+ 2206.07183v2, BE 1805.01016v3 and CLD 1204.6277v2, together with the listed Stacks tag pages. BE's continuous-metric flattening argument has finite continuous approximants and does not suffer from the exhibited pole obstruction. The task grant is recorded separately in the unindexed task passage below. Registration failure, documentary hashes and compilation have no bearing on this mathematical verdict.

passages.statement: For compact K, metrizable T, a map ρ:S→T and families F_s of continuous functions K→R∪{−∞} stable under addition of real constants, define F̃_t by pointwise decreasing-net limits f_i∈F_{s_i} with ρ(s_i)→t. Every decreasing net g_i∈F̃_{t_i}, with t_i→t, has its pointwise limit in F̃_t (BJ arXiv:1801.08229v4, Lemma 4.6).

For a projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, BJ numerical psh functions are generically finite decreasing-net limits of generically finite FS functions in rational bundles with convergent numerical classes. They have generically finite decreasing varying-class closure, rational FS approximation, addition, positive scaling, constants and finite maxima (BJ v4, Definitions 2.18 and 4.1; Theorems 4.5, 4.7 and 4.15).

On an integral projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, genuine psh functions are finite at function-field divisorial valuations, satisfy the generic-trivial maximum principle, are determined everywhere by their divisorial values, and satisfy every usc obstacle inequality established divisorially. On connected projective varieties PSH(0)=R (BJ v4, 4.12, 4.17 and 4.22–4.25).

On an integral projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, every homogeneous θ-psh function has decreasing homogeneous rational FS approximants in rational bundles converging numerically to θ. Every genuine θ-psh φ has the pointwise decomposition φ=sup_{λ<sup φ}(h_λ+λ), where h_λ is homogeneous θ-psh and h_λ+λ≤φ (BJ v4, 6.15–6.17 and 6.23–6.25).

For normal projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, an actual rational bundle B and an effective rational Cartier divisor E, a generically finite FS function φ on B satisfies φ≤log|s_E|+C for some real C if and only if it has an actual FS quotient φ−log|s_E| on B−E, with the same coefficient group (BJ v4, Lemma 2.23).

For integral projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, usc regularization of a bounded-above psh supremum preserves its divisorial values. For a numerical class with nonempty psh cone, EP is equivalent to compactness of the normalized cone in the divisorial topology (BJ v4, Theorems 5.6 and 5.11).

For smooth integral projective X over algebraically closed trivially valued k, assuming char k=0 or dim X≤2, every numerical class has EP; psef classes have genuine V_θ=P_θ(0) and compact normalized cones; effective rational Cartier divisor division holds for dominated genuine psh functions (BJ addendum arXiv:2206.07183v2, Theorem A and Corollaries 2.1–2.3).
passages.quote: Assume that X is smooth, and that char k = 0 or dim X ≤ 2.

passages.statement: For integral projective X over an algebraically closed trivially valued field, proper algebraic closed subsets are pluripolar and pluripolar sets are negligible. For an ample class satisfying EP, finite-dual-energy probability measures annihilate negligible Borel sets (BJ v4, 4.36, 5.3 and 13.2).

On projective schemes over complete non-Archimedean fields, including trivial valuations, semiample rational-bundle psh metrics admit decreasing smooth semipositive regularization. Continuous psh-regularizable mixed products extend uniquely under uniform-to-weak convergence, are positive and symmetric, use the original fundamental cycle and have raw intersection mass. Their model/Deligne compatibility identifies them with BJ continuous ample mixed products (BE arXiv:1805.01016v3, 7.14, 8.3–8.5 and 8.18; BJ v4, Remark 7.23).
passages.quote: Every psh metric φ on a semiample Q-line bundle L is psh-regularizable.

On boundaryless non-Archimedean analytic spaces, logarithms of analytic units are smooth with zero d′d′′; metric curvature in an invertible local frame is d′d′′log||s||^{-1}. Continuous local Bedford–Taylor products are unchanged by smooth harmonic additions. Poincaré–Lelong holds for locally integrable semimetrics and regular meromorphic sections (CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2, 8.8.5 and 18.1.2–18.1.6).

passages.statement: On a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme with an ample invertible sheaf, sufficiently positive twists of finite-type quasi-coherent sheaves are globally generated. On a proper scheme over a Noetherian ring, sufficiently positive ample twists of coherent sheaves have vanishing higher cohomology. On a proper scheme over a field, the Euler characteristic of a coherent sheaf twisted by powers of invertible sheaves is a numerical polynomial of total degree at most its support dimension (Stacks 01Q3(7), 0B5T(4) and 0BEM).

passages.statement: For a Noetherian ring, zero divisors on a module are exactly the union of its associated primes; finite modules have finitely many associated primes and admit finite prime filtrations. On a locally Noetherian scheme, a section of an invertible sheaf is regular precisely when it does not vanish at any associated point (Stacks 00LD, 00L9, 00L0 and 0B3Q).
